messages:
alex: Quick proposal — adopt a predictive launch-padding strategy for spot-backed inference fleets to smooth 30–90s microbursts without mass overprovisioning. Idea: use short-term traffic forecasts + rolling launch window to keep a small, transient cushion of warm nodes per AZ.

alex: Why: we've seen p95 token latency spikes during short bursty workloads where scaler detects demand, triggers launches, but instance boot + model load takes ~45–90s. Users see tail latency or we fall back to more expensive on-demand.

alex: Proposal details (config sketch):
```yaml
policy: predictive_padding
padding_percentile_window: 60s
padding_target_percentile: 95
max_padding_nodes_per_az: 3
launch_lead_time_ms: 45000 # observed avg launch+init
padding_eviction_timeout: 120s # shrink cushion when demand subsides
hedge_reserve: 1 # keep 1 non-spot fallback per az for immediate capacity
```

maria: is this basically warm standby but shorter lived? what's the delta vs current warm lanes? :thinking_face:

alex: yes similar but transient and driven by short-horizon prediction. Current warm lanes are long-lived (minutes->hours) and expensive. Predictive padding is 30–120s retention, reacts to queue slope not absolute queue.

maria: what's the expected cost bump? ballpark numbers please.

alex: rough calc from last 30 days traffic: 95th-percentile microbursts add ~2.8 GPU-minutes/min on average. If we keep 1 extra GPU cushion in 3 busy AZs for 2 mins during spikes, cost delta ~+5–8% vs today but we avoid 30–90s p95 latency regressions and on-demand fallbacks that cost way more. I'll produce a precise estimate.

dan: interruption handling? if padding nodes are spot and they get preempted during a burst we could be worse off.

alex: good catch. design includes: 1) prefer spot but keep hedge_reserve (config above) of non-spot fallback; 2) diversify AZs and instance types for padding; 3) quick re-schedule path: when a padded spot dies, immediately try another padded launch up to max_padding_nodes_per_az and fall back to hedge_reserve if failed. soft-drain on preemption to move in-progress KV caches if possible.

julie: what metrics/telemetry do we need to make this safe? Who owns them? :clipboard:

alex: at minimum: pending_request_count, p50/p95_queue_time, node_launch_latency (95th), spot_interruption_rate_by_az, model_warm_init_time. We also need a new event: padding_shrink/grow counts to debug oscillation.

kevin: infra can emit node_launch_latency and interruption_rate. we need an exporter update and a tag on padded nodes (`padding=true`). tagging should be quick.

kevin: question — do we plan to use ML forecasting or a heuristic slope-based predictor? Forecasting adds complexity and potential regression vector.

alex: start with a simple slope+EWMA predictor (detect sustained positive derivative over 15–30s) and keep ML model as opt-in later. simplicity first.

maria: rollout plan? canary regions? thresholds?

alex: canary: us-west-2 with conservative limits: max_padding_nodes_per_az=1, padding_target_percentile=90, and an aggressive shrink timeout of 60s. Observe for 2 weeks. If p95 latency drops >10% during bursts and cost delta <7% we'll expand.

ops-bot: Note: Please update the autoscaler runbook with steps to force-disable predictive padding and an emergency override flag `--disable-predictive-padding`.

julie: alerting changes: add alert if padding_eviction_rate > 20% in 5m window, or if node_launch_latency(95) > 120s for two consecutive windows. Also create a dashboard: "predictive-padding — cushion health".

kevin: infra action items: 1) tag padded nodes, 2) expose node_launch_latency metric (ETA 3d), 3) add small API to request immediate hedge (for SRE).

alex: dev action items: 1) implement slope predictor + policy toggle (ETA 1w), 2) integration tests for padding lifecycle (ETA 1w), 3) cost estimator job to show nightly cost delta (ETA 3d).

dan: can we reuse existing soft-drain code? if not, add to backlog. moving KV caches across nodes isn't trivial.

alex: we can reuse partial soft-drain for ephemeral work but full KV migration will be future work — for now prefer quick re-schedule and model-cache warming on new nodes.

sched-bot: Canary scheduled: predictive-padding rollout -> us-west-2 on 1718004834 by @alex. Rolling window: 2w monitor.

maria: acked. i want a daily digest for the canary: cost delta + p95 tail + interruption events.

alex: will add. i’ll post an initial cost sensitivity table tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: FYI — if we do this we should audit IAM roles for the autoscaler to ensure it can tag nodes and request hedge launches.

julie: i'll prep the dashboard template and alert runbook entries.

alex: final note: keep max_padding_nodes_per_az small to avoid wasting capacity; aim to let the hedging/reschedule system absorb most interruptions. this is an optimization for many short bursts that currently cause expensive fallbacks.

maria: sounds reasonable. excited to see the numbers.

alex: done for now. I'll follow up with the config PR and the cost table.
